doc.title: Jones Hank — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: A&R man Teddy Reig and Teddie's memory
summary: Jones recalls the heavy A&R man who worked for Savoy before Ozzie Cadena.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: My first record date: sessions, personnel, discography

blocks.x: I think Teddy Reed was one of the first…
Oh yeah, Teddy Reeds. Did you ever meet him?
No, but I think I know that name.

500 pounds, maybe less. He was so fat. He was the A&R man at one time for, I think, Riverside. That was before Orrin Keepnews came on. Maybe that was while Orrin Keepnews was there. But, he used to do some work for—What’s that other company?

Savoy, yes. But, there is also that other company…Okay, so it’s mainly Savoy. But, that was before Ozzie Cadena came along, you know? Teddie has a fantastic memory. She remembers telephone numbers from 1954! (Laughs)
It’s a little failing now. Sven: That’s alright (laughs).
He used to rely on me for it. He’d say, “Can you tell me what date this person did that, and they did this?" (Laughs)
